solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: T who's jumping on one foot

definitions.meaning: in this puzzle T stands for a thespian, here the film actor Dennis of that surname
someone who moves in little jumps on one leg

explanation.definitionFit: Dennis Hopper was an American screen actor, and one who hops along on one leg is literally a hopper.

clue.text: It stars Brody in Bantustan

definitions.meaning: the American TV thriller whose central character is Nicholas Brody
a territory set aside for Black South Africans under apartheid, a so-called national state

explanation.definitionFit: The TV thriller featuring Sergeant Brody shares its title with the apartheid word for a tribal reserve.

clue.text: Offer to tourists in group having time at port

parts.note: a pack is a group, as of wolves
an age is a long period
Deal is a port town in Kent, England

explanation.surface: Tourists in a party are kept waiting at a harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: A holiday sold with travel and lodging in one price is a classic offer to tourists.

clue.text: Test once before noon

parts.note: ex means former, as in an ex-wife
AM, ante meridiem, is the morning

explanation.surface: A test held at some time in the morning.
explanation.definitionFit: An exam is a formal test of knowledge, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: T remains on highland farm

parts.note: what is left after burning, as in ashes
a croft is a small tenant farm in the Scottish Highlands

explanation.surface: An actor's ashes are scattered on a small Scottish farm.
explanation.walkthrough: T throughout this puzzle stands for a thespian; here Dame Peggy Ashcroft, the English stage and screen actress.
explanation.definitionFit: Peggy Ashcroft was a celebrated English actress, so she fits the puzzle's recurring thespian.

clue.text: Inventory from editor in German school

indicators.note: the editor is placed within the German word

parts.note: Schule is German for school

explanation.surface: A list comes from an editor at a German school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal; 'German school' wants a German word, not a type of school.
explanation.definitionFit: A schedule can be a list or table of items, so it serves as an inventory.

clue.text: They are keen to advance, coming first in rushes

indicators.note: the ordinal is placed inside the word for rushes

parts.note: to career is to rush headlong
1st written with I for the figure one

explanation.surface: Ambitious people dash ahead, coming first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal; 'first' is written as the ordinal 1st, with I standing for the figure one, a common crossword trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Careerists are people intent on advancing their careers, often ruthlessly.

clue.text: Money for old rope. Easy — at first

indicators.note: only the opening letter of each of the three words is taken

explanation.surface: An easy earner, as the saying money for old rope goes.
explanation.walkthrough: Ore is a small coin of Sweden, Denmark and Norway. 'Money for old rope' is a British phrase for money easily earned.
explanation.definitionFit: The ore is a low-value Scandinavian coin, so it is a unit of money.

clue.text: 20's heartless flat dweller, say

indicators.note: without its heart, so the middle letter of the other answer goes

parts.note: the answer to 20 across, an actor's surname

explanation.surface: An actor without feeling lives in an apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' takes the middle N from TENNANT (20 across). 'say' marks a flat dweller as only one example of a tenant.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone renting a flat is an example of a tenant, an occupier who pays rent.

clue.text: Old car firm on outskirts of Orlando on motorway to Orlando

parts.note: BL is British Leyland, the defunct British carmaker

indicators.note: the outside letters of the place name are taken

parts.note: M marks a British motorway, as in the M1

explanation.surface: An old car maker sets up by a motorway near Orlando.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the surname that goes 'to Orlando' to make the actor Orlando Bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: Orlando Bloom is the English actor, so this surname is what attaches to the first name Orlando.

clue.text: T, man or child here, tipsy

indicators.note: being drunk suggests the letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: An actor, adult or youngster, is found here a little drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tipsy' rearranges the fourteen letters of 'man or child here' into the full name of the English actor Sir Michael Hordern.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Michael Hordern was a much-loved English character actor, matching the puzzle's thespian T.

clue.text: See 10
Seen mail returned close to T

indicators.note: sent back, so the words seen mail are read from the end

parts.note: next to, as in a house on the main road

explanation.surface: Letters arrive back near some person called T.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns SEENMAIL into LIAMNEES, and ON for 'close to' completes the Northern Irish actor's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Liam Neeson is a Northern Irish film actor, so he is one of the puzzle's thespians.

clue.text: T hailed drunk in flowing dress

indicators.note: the shuffled letters sit inside the garment

parts.note: a gown is a long flowing dress

indicators.note: intoxicated, so the letters of hailed reel into another order

explanation.surface: Someone tipsy was greeted while wearing a long gown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' makes LDIEHA and 'in' sets it within the garment; 'flowing dress' looks like description but is the outer piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Goldie Hawn is an American film actress, one of the puzzle's run of thespians.

clue.text: Arranged matinee chat — here?

indicators.note: set out in a new order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Fixed a chat at an afternoon showing, perhaps in a picture house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arranged' rearranges MATINEECHAT; the question mark flags 'here' as a place where a matinee would be shown.
explanation.definitionFit: A matinee is an afternoon screening, so the place it happens is a picture house.

clue.text: Grieving relative, we're told, bright early on

indicators.note: heard rather than read, signalling a sound-alike

parts.note: a son who is in mourning

explanation.surface: A grieving family member is said to be cheerful at dawn.
explanation.definitionFit: The early-day sun is bright first thing, which suits the description bright early on.

clue.text: See 12
Ts (Gould or Denholm) measure ten times

parts.note: an ell is an old measure of cloth length
the figures 1 and 0 read as the letters I and O
T is the abbreviation for time, so two of them make times

explanation.surface: Two actors measure something ten times over.
explanation.walkthrough: The surname fits both actors: Elliott Gould takes it as a forename, Denholm Elliott as a surname, hence 'Ts'.
explanation.definitionFit: Elliott Gould and Denholm Elliott were both screen actors, so the plural thespian covers either one.

clue.text: Mean and keen to embrace minister

indicators.note: the word for keen holds the other word inside it

parts.note: into means enthusiastic about, as in into jazz
to minister to is to tend, care for

explanation.surface: A clergyman is both stingy and eager to hug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to embrace' is the container signal; 'keen' means into, as in being into jazz, an informal usage.
explanation.definitionFit: To mean to do something is to plan it, the same sense as having that intention.

clue.text: Placated and imitated, eating vegetables

indicators.note: taking food in, so the word for imitated contains the other

parts.note: to ape is to copy
peas are green vegetables

explanation.surface: Someone was calmed and copied while eating greens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eating' is the container signal; 'Placated and imitated' reads like two definitions, but only the first defines.
explanation.definitionFit: To appease someone is to pacify or calm them, so placated is a synonym.

clue.text: Relative under canvas, as T

indicators.note: under canvas means camping, so the relative goes within the tent

parts.note: a tent is made of canvas
nan is a grandmother

explanation.surface: A family member is camping, like a certain actor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under' with 'canvas' gives the idiom under canvas, camping, so the relative sits inside the tent; the actor is David Tennant.
explanation.definitionFit: David Tennant is a Scottish stage and television actor, one of the puzzle's thespians.

clue.text: Holy man has to look back at T

parts.note: ST is short for saint

indicators.note: looking back suggests the word for look is read in reverse

parts.note: to peer is to look closely

explanation.surface: A holy man has to turn round and look at an actress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' makes REEP; the actress is Meryl Streep, and 'look back at' reads like a single phrase but splits into piece and signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Meryl Streep is an American film actress, one of the thespians this puzzle's T stands for.

clue.text: The French head drops point on Greek island

parts.note: les is a plural form of the in French

indicators.note: lets go of, so a letter is removed

parts.note: a boss is the head of a firm
S is a compass point, south

explanation.surface: A French chief loses a point while on a Greek island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drops' removes the compass point, leaving BOS; 'head drops' looks like a nod but head is the boss.
explanation.definitionFit: Lesbos is a large island in the Aegean Sea belonging to Greece.

clue.text: T mountaineer turning in bed, bra-less

indicators.note: tossing and turning, so the letters roll over into a new order

explanation.surface: An actor who climbs mountains tosses in bed without underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' rearranges the letters of 'in bed, bra-less' into the full name of the booming English actor, who also climbed mountains and attempted Everest.
explanation.definitionFit: Brian Blessed is an English actor and keen climber who tried Everest, so he is a thespian mountaineer.

clue.text: T (amateur detective) accepting books by Queen

indicators.note: taking in, so the detective's name holds the other letters

parts.note: Ellery Queen is the amateur sleuth of American detective fiction
NT is the New Testament, a set of books
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: An actor playing a sleuth takes on books alongside the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepting' is the container signal; 'Queen' doubles as a tease on the sleuth's surname, Ellery Queen, the amateur detective of American mystery novels.
explanation.definitionFit: Dame Ellen Terry was the leading Shakespearean actress of the Victorian stage, so a thespian.

clue.text: T Reid comes before November

definitions.meaning: the actor of that first name who played Frank Butcher in the British soap EastEnders
in the NATO phonetic alphabet the code word for M precedes November

explanation.definitionFit: Mike Reid was an EastEnders actor, and the radio code word for M directly precedes November.

clue.text: Earl turned over strange taro tuber

indicators.note: flipped round, so the word for strange is read backwards

parts.note: odd means peculiar

explanation.surface: A peer turned over an odd tropical root.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned over' makes DDO; 'strange taro' looks like an anagram cue but strange is simply odd.
explanation.definitionFit: Eddo is another name for the taro plant's edible corm, a starchy tropical root.

clue.text: See 23
Listener of The Archers

indicators.note: the run of letters comes out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone who tunes in to the long-running radio farm drama.
explanation.walkthrough: The Archers is a long-running BBC radio soap set in a farming village; the answer is inside 'The Archers'.
explanation.definitionFit: The organ of hearing is what does the listening, a common crossword sense.

clue.text: One garment for T

parts.note: an is the indefinite article, meaning one
a dress is an item of clothing

explanation.surface: A single item of clothing for an actor.
explanation.walkthrough: AN plus DRESS gives Ursula Andress, the Swiss actress of the first Bond film.
explanation.definitionFit: Ursula Andress is a Swiss film actress, one of the thespians in this puzzle.

clue.text: Offspring holding a coin for T

indicators.note: the son contains the other letters inside himself

parts.note: a son is a child
the rand is the currency of South Africa

explanation.surface: A child clutches a coin meant for some actor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' is the container signal; the rand is South Africa's currency, and the actress is Susan Sarandon.
explanation.definitionFit: Susan Sarandon is an American film actress, one of this puzzle's thespians.

clue.text: T at small house with drawback

parts.note: HO is the abbreviation for house
read as draw back, the word draw turned round

explanation.surface: An actor at a little home with a disadvantage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawback' looks like a disadvantage but splits as draw plus back, reversing draw; the actor is Trevor Howard of Brief Encounter.
explanation.definitionFit: Trevor Howard was an English film actor, so he fits the puzzle's thespian T.
